title: Extension of a specified partial cellular descent along a filtered root presentation
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be uncountable regular, meaning that a union of fewer than $\tau$ sets of size less than $\tau$ has size less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms admits a cocone; for a poset, every subset of size less than $\tau$, including the empty subset, must have an upper bound. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Use the cellular trees, their specified cell squares, and restricted colimits of [def-coef-good-cellular-tree].

Let $I$ be a small $\tau$-filtered poset, let $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram in $\mathcal A$, and fix a colimit cocone $v_i:V_i\to V$. Let $L$ be an arrow class and let $D$ be an $L$-tree rooted at $V$, on a small well-founded poset $T$ with $|T|<\tau$, with specified cells $c_t:P_t\to Q_t$. Assume each $P_t$ is $\tau$-presentable; no presentability of $Q_t$, $V_i$ or $V$ is assumed. Fix $i\in I$ and a downward-closed $E\subseteq T$. Suppose an $L$-tree $D^E$ rooted at $V_i$, on $E$ with the same specified cells, is given together with an isomorphism from its objectwise pushout along $v_i$ to $D|_E$. Such an isomorphism is under $V$ and respects every order arrow, the induced predecessor colimit maps, the attaching maps from $P_t$, and the maps from $Q_t$.

There exist $j\ge i$, an $L$-tree $D'$ on all of $T$ rooted at $V_j$ with the same specified cells, an isomorphism $D'|_E\cong D^E\amalg_{V_i}V_j$, and an isomorphism $D'\amalg_{V_j}V\cong D$. Both isomorphisms respect every order arrow and both legs of every specified cell square. On $E$ their composite is the given pushout identification for $D^E$, using the canonical iterated-pushout identification. Here objectwise pushout means replacing each object $W$ under a root $R$ by $W\amalg_R R'$ along the stated root map $R\to R'$.

Agent-formulated relative version starting from a specified lower subtree, using only presentability of cell sources; read online 2026-10-17. Not archived in literature/. proof.text: Write $B_{R,S}(W)=W\amalg_R S$ for root change. A map from this pushout to $Z$ is precisely a pair $W\to Z$, $S\to Z$ agreeing on $R$. Thus a cocone under $S$ from the root-changed restriction is exactly a cocone under $R$ from the original restriction with the chosen map $S\to Z$. This proves preservation of restricted colimits, including the empty one. For a cell square, maps out of $(Y\amalg_P Q)\amalg_R S$ and out of $(Y\amalg_R S)\amalg_P Q$ are the same triples of maps from $Y,Q,S$, agreeing on $P$ and $R$. Hence the specified cell remains a pushout with $P,Q$ unchanged. For $R\to S\to S'$ the same calculation gives $(W\amalg_R S)\amalg_S S'\cong W\amalg_R S'$. All these isomorphisms commute with every defining leg; their composites agree because maps out of a colimit are determined by those legs.

source.place: Remark A.1.5.3 and Notation A.1.5.2, printed p. 800; universal-property expansion of root change

proof.text: Starting from $E$, repeatedly adjoin a minimal remaining element $t_\gamma$ and take unions at limits, obtaining downward-closed $E_\gamma$ and $E_\beta=T$. This stops with $\beta<\tau$: otherwise the distinct choices for $\gamma<\tau$ inject $\tau$ into $T$. Every predecessor of $t_\gamma$ is in $E_\gamma$. Construct increasing $i_\gamma$ and trees $D^\gamma$ on $E_\gamma$ under $V_{i_\gamma}$. Retain isomorphisms $\theta_{\delta\gamma}:B_{V_{i_\delta},V_{i_\gamma}}D^\delta\cong D^\gamma|_{E_\delta}$ for $\delta\le\gamma$, and $\psi_\gamma:B_{V_{i_\gamma},V}D^\gamma\cong D|_{E_\gamma}$. Require $\theta_{\delta\eta}$ to equal $\theta_{\gamma\eta}\circ B\theta_{\delta\gamma}$ after Step 1's associativity, and require the $\psi$ to commute with these comparisons. All are isomorphisms of trees, including both cell legs. Start with $i_0=i$, $D^0=D^E$, identity $\theta_{00}$ and the supplied $\psi_0$. These stronger comparison data make the eventual identification on $E$ prescribed rather than merely existent.

source.place: Lemma A.1.5.11, data (a)-(c), zero stage and well-founded exhaustion, printed pp. 806-807

proof.text: At a successor let $t=t_\gamma$, $B=\{s:s<t\}\subseteq E_\gamma$, $a=i_\gamma$, and let $Y$ be the predecessor colimit of $D^\gamma|_B$ under $V_a$. Step 1 and $\psi_\gamma$ identify $D(B)$ with $Y\amalg_{V_a}V$. The tail $I_{\ge a}$ is small and $\tau$-filtered: adjoin $a$ to any fewer-than-$\tau$ indices and choose an upper bound. The cocone $W_j=Y\amalg_{V_a}V_j\to Y\amalg_{V_a}V$ on this tail is colimiting. Indeed, maps $W_j\to Z$ compatible in $j$ are exactly a single map $Y\to Z$ and compatible maps $V_j\to Z$ agreeing on $V_a$; the maps from $Y$ coincide since $a$ is the tail's least element. To extend the latter family to any $V_k$, choose $j\ge k,a$ and compose $V_k\to V_j\to Z$. Another choice gives the same map by passage to a common upper bound; this also verifies compatibility for $k\le k'$. The colimit property of $V$ now gives exactly a map $Y\amalg_{V_a}V\to Z$, uniquely. This proves the tail-colimit identification without a cofinality assumption left implicit.

source.place: Lemma A.1.5.11, successor-stage tail-colimit argument, printed p. 807

proof.text: The definition of $\tau$-presentability of $P_t$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P_t,D(B))$ with the colimit of $\operatorname{Hom}(P_t,W_j)$ over this small $\tau$-filtered tail. Apply clause (1) of the filtered-colimit-of-sets node to the specified attaching map $P_t\to D(B)$. It is represented by $b_t:P_t\to W_j$ for some $j\ge a$, and its composite to $D(B)$ equals the specified map, not just an isomorphic choice. This uses no presentability of $Q_t$ or any root.

source.place: Lemma A.1.5.11, factorization of the attaching map through one filtered stage, printed p. 807

proof.text: Set $i_{\gamma+1}=j$. On $E_\gamma$ use $B_{V_a,V_j}D^\gamma$; at $t$ take $W_j\amalg_{P_t}Q_t$ with its specified cell square. For $s<t$ the order map is the composite from the $s$ vertex to the predecessor colimit $W_j$ and then to this pushout. There is no old vertex above $t$ since $E_\gamma$ is downward-closed. The cocone identities prove functoriality. Step 1 identifies the predecessor colimit and proves that after root change to $V$ this new square is the original square. The resulting isomorphism at $t$ is the unique one commuting with the predecessor and $Q_t$ legs, and agrees with old order maps by their factorization through the predecessor colimit. Keep $\psi_\gamma$ on old vertices. Define all $\theta_{\delta,\gamma+1}$ by root change of $\theta_{\delta\gamma}$ and associativity. Their coherence and compatibility with $\psi$ follow on every defining leg from Step 1, so the induction invariant persists.

source.place: Lemma A.1.5.11, successor pushout and compatibility clauses, printed p. 807

proof.text: At a nonzero limit $\lambda\le\beta$ choose an upper bound $i_\lambda$ of the fewer-than-$\tau$ indices $i_\gamma$, $\gamma<\lambda$. For each $s\in E_\lambda$ let $b(s)<\lambda$ be its first stage of occurrence, and define its new vertex as $B_{V_{i_{b(s)}},V_{i_\lambda}}D^{b(s)}(s)$. For any later $\gamma<\lambda$ containing $s$, $\theta_{b(s),\gamma}$ and Step 1 give an identification with the root-changed $\gamma$ vertex. Coherence of $\theta$ says these identifications agree after every further stage. Define an order map using a stage containing both endpoints; define a cell square at $s$ using stage $b(s)$. Such a stage contains every predecessor of $s$ since it is downward-closed. Independence of the stage follows from $\theta$ on order arrows and both cell legs. Functoriality is checked in one stage containing any three vertices. The entire predecessor diagram at $s$ is therefore isomorphic to its root-changed diagram at $b(s)$; Step 1 proves that its specified square is still a pushout. These same identifications define $\theta_{\gamma\lambda}$; root-changing the earlier $\psi$ gives $\psi_\lambda$, independent of the choice by their compatibility. Their coherence is checked on each vertex using a common stage below $\lambda$. This constructs the limit tree and all induction data, rather than assuming gluing from agreement only over $V$. At the final stage set $j=i_\beta$, $D'=D^\beta$. Then $\theta_{0\beta}^{-1}$ and $\psi_\beta$ are the requested isomorphisms. Their compatibility with $\psi_0$ is exactly the prescribed condition on $E$.

source.place: Lemma A.1.5.11, limit-stage gluing and conclusion, printed p. 807

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-cd6173492 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full. The statement is true. Hand-tested cases: E=T gives beta=0 and psi_0; T empty is trivial; E empty is the citer's use in lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation; one cell factors P->V through V_j; two incomparable cells also hold. Steps 1, 3 and 5 are correct universal-property calculations (pushouts and undercategory colimits, the tail colimit over I_{>=a}, and the successor pushout giving D(t) through D's specified square). Step 2 sets up the induction explicitly: a minimal-element exhaustion that ends at beta<tau, coherent theta and psi, and the base case. Step 4 uses only tau-presentability of P_t, and clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise applies on the small tau-filtered tail. Step 6 bounds fewer than tau indices, takes each vertex at its first stage, and gets the prescribed composite on E from psi compatibility. Citations (def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-coef-good-cellular-tree, the Mathlib leaf) say what the steps use. There is no cycle, no off-route statement, no new node, and tool_uses=[] is correct. Duplicate check: lem-coef-small-cellular-tree-descent assumes a locally presentable category and presentable endpoints and has no specified lower subtree. The approximations, subset-enlargement and presentable-vertices nodes are different statements. Blueprint from/same_as is consistent with the parent. HTT A.1.5.11 is not archived under literature/, so the source place could not be checked against the text; the item marks the proof agent-formulated, and the argument stands on its own. No fixes.
